title: Dynamic prefetch gating and hierarchical fallback lane for memory-aware continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and aggressive KV prefetching scale across long-context chat workloads we observe transient GPU OOMs and forced request failures during peak windows. Existing mitigations (prefetch backoff and model fallback) are coarse-grained and sacrifice a lot of quality for a single request rather than enabling graceful degradation.

Goal: Implement a memory-aware runtime layer that 1) dynamically gates KV prefetch and batch admission based on live GPU occupancy and token urgency, 2) performs staged KV spill and partial-quant/model degradation in a ranked fallback lane, and 3) preserves latency SLOs via hedged retries and short-circuit completion strategies. This mechanism should reduce hard OOMs, lower failed request rate under pressure, and provide measurable trade-offs between token-quality and completion success.

Design summary:
- Urgency-weighted token triage: each incoming request carries a computed urgency score (derived from RL-derived heuristics and simple heuristics for latency-sensitive routes). Low-urgency tokens are candidates for trimmed prefix prefetch and later progressive completion.
- Prefetch gating window: continuous batching admission includes a short rolling window (50-200ms) that uses GPU resident memory watermark + inflight KV reservations to accept/reject prefetches. When occupancy > gate_threshold we only admit high-urgency requests and convert others into "deferred" mode.
- Hierarchical fallback lane (HFL): a multi-stage degradation pipeline with explicit checkpoints: (1) hot-KV keep + cold-KV on CPU (async spill), (2) token-priority shedding (drop low-utility context tokens), (3) micro-quant model offload (8-bitFP or int4 micro-variant), (4) micro-model stub (shorter-context tiny model) to finish tokens. Each stage records a deterministic downgrade tag so downstream billing/analytics can attribute quality loss.
- Staged CPU-KV spill: implement snapshot-based async spill of least-recently-used KV shards to host memory with a fast async fetch-on-demand path and conservative prefetch for hot keys. Spill uses a soft quota to avoid excessive PCIe thrash.
- Hedged retries + short-circuit completions: for requests demoted to HFL we may issue parallel micro-variant hedged calls at reduced token budgets with a fast winner-takes-all policy to maintain p95/p99 SLOs. Short-circuiting returns partial structured outputs when full-context generation would otherwise fail.

Telemetry & metrics: track OOM per-GPU, degraded_completions_count, degraded_success_rate, p99 latency by degradation stage, percentage of requests admitted to deferred mode, and average token quality delta via eval prompts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hard OOM rate on canary fleet reduced >= 75% under synthetic pressure tests.
- Failed-completions due to memory reduced >= 60% with no more than 15% of requests routed to HFL in steady state.
- p95 latency regression <= 20ms for high-urgency paths.
- Rollout controlled by runtime-1.19 release flags and observability dashboards that surface downgrade tags and customer-impact signals.

2025-02-18 - Design review (notes): Decided on urgency-weighted triage (simple linear combination of route SLA, tokens-left, and historical latency). Priya approved approach.
2025-02-21 - Marco Li: WIP integration test harness for simulated PCIe spill and synthetic memory pressure; initial results show reduced OOMs but increased p99 on deferred requests.
2025-02-24 - Engineering review: Feedback to add conservative prefetch retry backoff and a limit on host-memory spill requests per-GPU to avoid thrashing.
